review_scope: first-hour precipitation map rendering, retained arrays, receipt, color scale, and coordinate selection

findings.finding: The geographic aspect correction is inverted. Matplotlib numeric aspect is y-unit/x-unit; to make longitude distances shorter by cos(latitude), the intended aspect is 1/cos(mean_lat). The current cos(mean_lat) expands the longitude dimension and distorts the plotted spatial pattern horizontally.

Square scatter markers may overlap neighboring retained grid points and make the sampled mask/precipitation edges appear broader than their point support. Treat the map as sampled point visualization, not area coverage or polygon boundaries; reduce marker size if a closer cell-footprint rendering is desired.
RN1 zero/trace values are shown gray, but the retained artifact has no coverage/QC mask; gray is not evidence of observed dry conditions. The receipt and report state this limitation.

checks_passed: NPZ declares 12:00–13:00 UTC under supplied one-hour/mm RN1 convention.
NPZ reference, forecasts, coordinates, and flat indexes match the source aligned NPZ and fixed mask selection; no row/column reversal found.
Fields and maxima are finite and nonnegative; maxima are below 100 mm, so the over-range color is unused.
BoundaryNorm and nine-color palette map [0,0.1), [0.1,0.5), [0.5,1), [1,2.5), [2.5,5), [5,10), [10,20), [20,50), [50,100), with >=100 over; tick labels match those intervals.
